Cristiano Ronaldo sent his penalty attempt wide as United failed to take an early lead at the Nou Camp. The Portugal winger, the top scorer in this season's competition, spurned the chance to net for the 39th time overall this campaign and give United a vital away goal. The 23-year-old hit the stanchion high outside goalkeeper Victor Valdes' left-hand post in the third minute after Gabriel Milito handled his header from a Paul Scholes corner. It was United's best chance in a game dominated by the home side, who had the best of possession with some silky moves but failed to find the killer pass in the final third of the pitch. United goalkeeper Edwin van der Sar made a string of saves, especially in the second half, but was not often seriously tested. Barcelona were boosted by the return of Argentina forward Lionel Messi, who started alongside Samuel Eto'o up front, with Thierry Henry on the bench after also being cleared following an illness. Messi picked out Samuel Eto'o in the 13th minute only for midfielder Scholes -- making his 100th Champions League appearance -- to make a vital interception. Barcelona pressed forward again in the 21st minute and Rafael Marquez got clear of his marker but his header failed to trouble Van der Sar, who was back in the side following a groin injury. Then Yaya Toure showed good skill for the home side and sent a good cross into the area that was turned away by Van der Sar. Ronaldo felt he should have had another penalty in the 30th minute when he was bundled over by Marquez after Xavi had carelessly lost possession, but Swiss referee Massimo Busacca allowed play to continue. Eto'o rattled in a shot after 34 minutes but Wes Brown -- who passed a late fitness test to replace the ill Nemanja Vidic in central defense -- made a vital block. Brown partnered Rio Ferdinand, with England midfielder Owen Hargreaves operating as a makeshift right-back. Deco, starting his first game for Barcelona after two months out with injuries, then failed to test Van der Sar with a free-kick in the 38th minute. Marquez was booked in the 44th minute after tripping Ronaldo as he attempted to surge forward, meaning the Mexican is suspended for next Tuesday's second leg at Old Trafford. Ronaldo sent his effort from an acute angle wide of the post. After the break, Messi saw his effort blocked in the 47th minute and then Van der Sar tipped over defender Gianluca Zambrotta's long-range effort. Messi beat three United players but Ferdinand cut out his low cross from the right, then he played in a superb ball for Eto'o -- who lashed his shot against the side-netting. Deco tested Van der Sar with a low drive, then the Dutchman easily dealt with a 20-yard effort from Xavi. Barcelona coach Frank Rijkaard took off Messi in the 62nd minute, replacing him with teenager Bojan Krkic, who scored the winner in the first leg of the quarterfinal against Schalke. A foul on the Serbian-born Spaniard drew a yellow card for Hargreaves in the 73rd minute, then United boss Alex Ferguson bolstered his midfield by bringing on Nani for England forward Wayne Rooney -- who had started up front with Carlos Tevez. Rijkaard responded by replacing Deco with Henry in the 77th minute, and the French forward forced a scrambled save by Van der Sar with a long-range shot on 83. Ferguson brought on veteran winger Ryan Giggs for Tevez soon after, then Van der Sar denied Andres Iniesta and also dived to comfortably save Henry's free-kick from 35 yards. Barcelona continued to press until the final whistle, but still could not create a clear-cut opportunity. E-mail to a friend .

He still won fouls, carried the ball dangerously and unsettled defenders, but the missed penalty hung over his night.

### Messi bright but carefully managed

For Barcelona, Messi was the main source of unpredictability. Starting on the right but drifting into central pockets, he repeatedly looked to drive at United’s compact defensive block. His acceleration caused moments of alarm, particularly when he cut inside onto his stronger left foot, but United’s midfield and back four worked hard to deny him clean shooting lanes.

Messi’s involvement was carefully monitored. Having recently returned from injury, he showed flashes of brilliance without quite sustaining his influence over the full contest. Frank Rijkaard eventually withdrew him in the second half, a substitution that reflected both fitness management and Barcelona’s need to alter the attacking picture. The decision removed Barcelona’s most explosive individual threat, though the hosts continued to probe through Xavi, Deco and Andrés Iniesta.

### Van der Sar calm under pressure

While Barcelona had the majority of possession, United goalkeeper Edwin van der Sar was a composed and important figure. He was not subjected to a barrage of clear one-on-one chances, but his handling, positioning and authority were vital on a night when Barcelona delivered dangerous balls into the box and tried to create openings through intricate combinations.

Van der Sar’s experience showed in the way he slowed the tempo when required and brought calm to United’s defensive shape. In front of him, Rio Ferdinand and Wes Brown defended with concentration, while Patrice Evra and Owen Hargreaves had demanding assignments against Barcelona’s wide movement and overlapping full-backs.

United’s plan relied on discipline: compress the space between midfield and defence, prevent Messi and Iniesta from receiving freely between the lines, and then look for Ronaldo, Wayne Rooney or Carlos Tevez in transition. It was not a display of attacking ambition, but it was highly controlled.

### Tactical battle: Barcelona possession, United restraint

Barcelona dominated the ball for long periods, with Xavi dictating tempo and Iniesta drifting intelligently across midfield. Yaya Touré provided balance at the base of midfield, while Deco pushed forward to add pressure around United’s penalty area.

However, Barcelona often struggled to turn possession into clear chances. United defended narrow, leaving little room for quick combinations around the edge of the box. Paul Scholes and Michael Carrick sat deep, Park Ji-sung worked tirelessly to close passing lanes, and Rooney was asked to contribute heavily without the ball, often tracking back to support the full-back areas.

Ferguson’s tactical approach was pragmatic. After Ronaldo’s penalty miss, United appeared increasingly content to avoid defeat rather than chase the game. The visitors rarely committed numbers forward, preferring to preserve defensive balance and trust that the second leg at Old Trafford would offer a better platform.

Rijkaard, meanwhile, tried to inject freshness from the bench as Barcelona searched for a late winner. The changes altered personnel but not the central pattern: Barcelona had the ball, United had the structure.

### Substitutions alter the rhythm

Barcelona made attacking changes in the second half, including the introduction of **Bojan Krkić**, whose movement and youthful energy offered a different profile in the final third. **Thierry Henry** was also introduced, adding experience and a more direct goal threat against tiring defenders. Late changes were designed to increase Barcelona’s presence around the box, but United’s defensive line held firm.

United’s substitutions were more conservative in tone. **Nani** came on to provide fresh legs and an outlet on the flank, while **Ryan Giggs** added experience and ball retention late in the game. Ferguson also looked to protect his midfield and manage the closing stages, ensuring Barcelona were not given space to exploit as the match opened up.

The benches reflected the contrasting priorities: Barcelona chased a home advantage; United protected an away draw.

### Bookings and physical edge

The match was not overly violent, but it carried the tension of a Champions League semi-final. Barcelona defenders were forced into several tactical fouls as Ronaldo looked to break into space, and United’s midfielders also had to tread carefully as they disrupted Barcelona’s rhythm.

**Rafael Márquez** was among the notable Barcelona players booked, a caution that carried added importance because of suspension concerns. The Mexican defender’s physical duel with Ronaldo and United’s attackers was a recurring feature. United also had players cautioned as the game became increasingly tactical, with fouls used to halt transitions and prevent either side from building momentum.

The bookings contributed to the sense of caution in the final stages. Neither team wanted to risk losing a player or leaving the tie exposed before the return leg.

### What the result means

The 0-0 draw leaves the semi-final finely balanced. Barcelona will feel they controlled enough of the match to deserve a goal, but they failed to test Van der Sar as frequently as their possession suggested they should. United, meanwhile, will regret Ronaldo’s missed penalty but can take satisfaction from their defensive discipline and the absence of an away goal conceded.

For Ronaldo, the night was one of frustration: a huge early chance missed, followed by limited service. For Messi, it was a performance of promise rather than dominance, full of dangerous bursts but ultimately contained by United’s collective organisation.

The tie now moves to Old Trafford, where United will expect to be more adventurous. Barcelona, denied at the Nou Camp, must find a way to convert possession into penetration if they are to reach the final.
